title: subpoena witness line
description: One line of witness output: one exec as the kernel saw it, one file change under a watched root, or a record that opens or closes a capture window. A line with a record field is a record, one with a file_op field a file change, and any other line an exec. See docs/ports.md (W, W7). Readers ignore fields they do not know; existing fields keep their name and meaning.

time.description: When the exec or file change was seen (for a file change, when the witness read it), or the record written (RFC 3339, UTC).

pid.description: PID in the process's own PID namespace.

ppid.description: Parent PID in the process's own PID namespace.

host_pid.description: PID in the initial PID namespace.

comm.description: Kernel task name, at most 15 bytes.

exe.description: The path passed to execve; may be relative.

cgroup.description: cgroup path without the hierarchy root, root-most first, at most 8 elements, such as subpoena/<trace id>.

trace_id.description: The session's trace ID, read from its cgroup name. Present only for execs inside a session cgroup, and absent on a file change from a tier-1 witness, which belongs to every trace.

attribution.description: How the line was tied to a trace. cgroup: present exactly when trace_id is. root: a file change seen under a watched root, returned for every trace.

record.description: start: the witness is attached and capturing. stop: it has stopped; healthy says whether the capture between start and stop is complete.

healthy.description: On a stop record: true only if no kernel events were lost and no read or write failed.

error.description: On an unhealthy stop record: what went wrong.

path.description: The absolute path changed, spelled from the root as it was given.

root.description: The watched root path is under.

source.description: inotify: the kernel queued the event. scan: a scan of a new directory found the entry; file_op is create whatever was done to it.

rename.description: Which side of a rename path is.

cookie.description: Ties the two sides of a rename; absent when zero.

roots.description: On a file witness's start record: the directories it watched.

coverage.description: On a file witness's stop record: what the capture might have missed even when healthy, in one line.
